# R391 — gated-region alias independent source audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only audit of `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-prefill-gated-region-alias-20261013`, HEAD `fd595aa7ef34bc04d16c2f385f0d62f09c8f3adc`, against parent `fd595aa7ef34bc04d16c2f385f0d62f09c8f3adc`. Audited only the supplied five dirty files and the named existing implementation report, R388, R389 v2, and registry v191. No source edits, builds, tests, GPU/runtime/process work, Git mutations, broad environment search, or cleanup were performed. The forbidden `prefill-gemm-only-contract-root-v1/record.json` was not read. Only this report was written.

## Finding

I found no new source-specific defect, undefined behavior, or gate-versus-region range mismatch in the audited implementation. This is an independent static-source conclusion only; all execution, fitting, parity, and performance remain unverified.

`STRATA_PREFILL_GATED_ALIAS` is frozen by a function-local static and enables only for the exact string `1`. `validate_gated_alias()` requires the existing frozen scratch alias in both `init` and `bytes_needed`; `init` rejects nonpositive chunks/checked extent overflow and checks the actual compute queue's `in_order` property before its first allocation. The ordinary absent/other-value behavior remains OFF. The new gate extent calculation also occurs in the count path under the same condition.

The normal HC path in `Prefill::run` submits down projection, SiLU, up projection to `m.gated`, injection projection to the separate `m.inj`, and then `gr_mix_r`'s full gate read on `m.cs`; the subsequent attention/MoE block's first region writer is enqueued afterward. The second HC half repeats this sequence. The gate has no other normal-path reader in the audited source. `Gemm` is initialized on the same passed stream, and native kernels receive `m.cs`. SYCL 2020 specifies that `property::queue::in_order` makes commands execute in submission order as if each depended on the previous command on that queue; it explicitly makes no ordering guarantee across queues. Thus the source's same-queue requirement supports this lifetime argument, while runtime execution is still untested. Official primary specification: [Khronos SYCL 2020, queue in_order property](https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html).

The other lifetimes are separated in the source. `R`, `xn16`, and injection remain distinct. PLE batched scratch and `draft_kv` use local subviews of `m.region` before/independently of the normal HC gate lifetime; they do not dereference the persistent `m.gated` pointer. `m.region_bytes` remains `block_max`, preserving the former PLE/draft batch and fallback decisions if gate extent enlarges the backing. `relayout()` drains compute and copy queues before calling common `carve()` again, so the alias view is rebuilt for the new borrowed base and chunk. MTP/draft's own local gate is separately carved from the same region and its gate producer/consumer are queued on `m.cs`.

## Range and count review

The production helper's `take_bytes()` reproduces the prior `Alloc::take` request rule, `(elements * element_bytes + 511) & ~255`, with checked multiplication/addition. `advance()` checks cumulative overflow, respects bounded borrowed capacity, and leaves cursor and offset unchanged on a short-cap failure. `region_layout()` computes `block_max=max(gdn,qsa,moe)`, gate extent with the same padded take rule, and `region_extent=max(block_max,gate_extent)` only when aliasing is active. The outer shared allocation is itself padded using the same rule; `gate_view()` verifies the gate extent fits the backing and returns its base. The nested GDN/QSA/MoE carvings each receive the actual `region_extent` capacity. Count and carve both use this layout, while `bytes_needed()` and `carve()` omit the same separate gate take under the same frozen flag. The fixed QSA batch values passed to count (256 and 32) match `Impl` defaults used in carve. No source-level count/carve or gate-range mismatch found.

The CPU fixture calls the same production host-only `exact_one`, `product`, `take_bytes`, `advance`, `region_layout`, and `gate_view` helpers; its ON/OFF, G<B/G=B/G>B, padding, cursor, bounded view, short-cap, overflow, shrink/regrow, and stock-12K cases therefore do test production helper behavior. It does not call production `Alloc::take`, full `Prefill::bytes_needed`/`carve`/`relayout`, device allocations, or queue work. Its synthetic owned-request ledger is not evidence of production ownership/free lifecycle or actual pointer aliasing. The fixture was not run.

Trace under `STRATA_TRACE` and required scratch alias reports both calculated extents, winner, actual allocated region request, total requested count, pointer values and equality. This is useful runtime evidence but source inspection alone cannot establish those addresses or a complete successful owned/borrowed lifecycle. The gate metric is the padded request, not usable payload or physical VRAM reclaimed. The reported 503,316,736 B is gate extent (503,316,480 B payload plus 256 B padding); when `block_max` exceeds that extent, deleting the separate take changes the source requested total by exactly 503,316,736 B. If gate exceeds block maximum, the helper enlarges region backing and reports the correspondingly smaller net saving.

## Capacity boundary and disposition

Using the supplied actual-12K capacity evidence, requested bytes change from 4,886,504,448 to 4,383,187,712 B. Against the supplied second free-memory observation of 4,422,336,512 B, the arithmetic margin is 39,148,800 B (about 37.3 MiB). This is only a comparison of requested count and one free-memory observation; it establishes neither physical fit nor runtime admission, and says nothing about quality, speed, or peak allocations.

Prior implementation report `implementation-gated-region-alias-v1.txt`, R388, R389 v2 and registry v191 were consulted to avoid repeating their already recorded implementation and lifecycle coverage. This report adds no runtime qualification or validation status. Default OFF remains in source. No recommendation to enable by default follows from this audit.
